note: A CENSUS OF THE LIVE CHAIN -- an independent oracle for the "accountability of
hand-picked arbiters" cut. This is NOT a list written here and not a retelling of
the script: it is what Base Sepolia answers to the question "which selectors are
mounted on the old ArbiterRegistryFacet". The cut's lists
(script/UpgradeArbiterAccountability.s.sol) are checked AGAINST IT rather than
against themselves.
WHY. Replace reverts on an unmounted selector, Add on a mounted one. An error
either way rejects the WHOLE cut in one production transaction, after both facets
have already been deployed. Before this file there was nothing to check the split
against: the test benches derived "what is mounted on chain" from the very list
they were checking -- a lock that looks at itself in the mirror.
HOW TO RETAKE IT. Literally, with the command in the command field below. It is a
read, not a transaction, so no key is needed. The RPC endpoint comes from an
environment variable and never reaches the file. Once retaken, update block,
takenAt and selectors in one commit; changing one alone is not allowed, because
the header has to describe precisely these lines.
AFTER THE CUT this file becomes a record of the past: the old facet empties out and
its 64 selectors scatter across two new addresses. There is no need to rewrite it
after the fact -- take a new census in a new file instead.
WHO IT WAS TAKEN FOR. The `forScript` field below names the cut script this census
validates, and the bench compares it against the VALUE taken from the script under
test itself (UpgradeArbiterAccountability.scriptPath()) rather than against a
literal. The real trap is not "the census is stale" but "an old census was taken
for a NEW script": a new script names itself differently, and the bench goes red
deterministically, without touching the network.
